sources: UKMTO Warning 187-26 via Al Jazeera liveblog (00:07 GMT Oct 30 = 04:07 ) + Reuters carry via investinglive (00:12 GMT = 04:12 ) + Arab News (05:10 Oct 30)
fault_line: Another burning ship, still no name and no cause: is Hormuz now a place where ships burn and nobody can say why — or is the fog itself the weapon?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT - UKMTO warning; cause, vessel identity and responsibility UNATTRIBUTED] UKMTO received a third-party report that a vessel transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was on fire about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman. UKMTO said the cause was unknown at time of report, and the status of the crew, damage assessment and environmental impact were unknown. UKMTO advised vessels to transit with caution. No vessel type, flag, cargo, casualty or cause is stated; there is no claim of responsibility and no indication whether the fire resulted from attack, accident or mechanical failure.
sections.what_verified: 2 declared families: UKMTO (T1, primary issuer of the warning) + Reuters (T1 wire carry). Al Jazeera (T2) carries the same warning text and does not add an independent confirmation. Corroboration here is the warning's issuance, not the fire's cause.
sections.what_disputed: WARNING-NUMBER CAUTION: this is Warning 187-26, a different number and a different position (25 nm NE of Khasab) from Warning 186-26 (0400-01: tanker struck by unknown projectile, 1600 GMT Oct 29) and from the 9 nm north-of-Khasab dhow fire/sinking reported Oct 29 — but UKMTO names no vessel in any of them, so a definitive vessel-level merge or split cannot be proved from the warnings alone. Do NOT merge 187-26 into the 186-26 projectile count, the dhow fire, or the IRGC's 3+1 mine claims; AP itself noted it was not immediately clear whether an Oct 29 burning vessel was one of the IRGC's three. The IRGC-mine vs CENTCOM-clearance dispute does not explain a fire of unknown cause.
sections.why_matters: A SECOND Hormuz warning in 24 hours — this time a ship on fire 25 miles off Oman, cause unknown: UKMTO confirms the fire, names no ship, blames no one. Two warnings, zero answers.
sections.context: Background: NEW IN-WINDOW WARNING -- UKMTO Warning 187-26: vessel on fire 25 nm northeast of Khasab, Oman, on outbound Hormuz transit; cause unknown, crew/damage/environment unknown

totw_analysis: Our read: A SECOND Hormuz warning in 24 hours — this time a ship on fire 25 miles off Oman, cause unknown: UKMTO confirms the fire, names no ship, blames no one. Two warnings, zero answers. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Another burning ship, still no name and no cause: is Hormuz now a place where ships burn and nobody can say why — or is the fog itself the weapon?
